title: What a two-week design sprint actually produces
ex: A prototype, five user sessions, and a build estimate you can take to your board.
body:
"Design sprint" has become a vague term. Here's precisely what ours produces in two weeks, so you can decide whether it's worth it.

## Week one

Monday and Tuesday are interviews: your team, then five people who'd use the product. Wednesday we map the core flow on a wall (or a FigJam board). Thursday and Friday are sketching, in low fidelity, on purpose.

## Week two

Monday to Wednesday we build a clickable prototype of the one flow that matters most. Thursday we test it with five users, recorded. Friday we write up what happened and what we'd change.

## What you leave with

- A Figma prototype you can put in front of investors or your board.
- Five recorded user sessions and a two-page summary.
- A build estimate for a first version, in weeks and cost, with the assumptions written down.
- An honest answer on whether to build it at all.

> About one sprint in four ends with "don't build this yet". That's the sprint paying for itself.
